newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda's profits rev up, Mazda gets back on track.
newsitem.headline: Honda's profits rev up, Mazda gets back on track.

text.p: Honda Motor Co. said Friday that its profits increased four-fold in the first six months of the year to a record $623 million.
Mazda Motor Corp., meanwhile, said it returned to profitability after a string of first-half losses in recent years.

Honda, which has been shedding its image as a maker of small cars for that of a manufacturer of recreation vehicles, said it posted a record parent current profit of 69.2 billion yen ($623 million) for the six months ended Sept. 30 -- four times higher than the year earlier period.
"The domestic car market is better than expected, and we got help from the weaker yen," Yoshihide Munekuni, executive vice president of the third-ranked Japanese automaker told reporters.
Mazda, Japan's fifth-largest car maker, also benefited from the weak yen, which makes Japanese goods more cost-competitive abroad.
Mazda said it managed a parent current profit of 2.08 billion yen ($18.7 million) for the period.

Mazda, whose range of models has failed to excite Japanese customers at a time when its competitors are coming up with a host of popular new models, had posted first-half losses for three straight years.
Honda, meanwhile, has been benefiting from a recreational vehicle boom in Japan.
The popularity of RVs, which now account for about half of Honda's car sales in Japan, helped raise its vehicle sales for the April-September period by 22.3 percent.
